answer: Sybil attackers need identities that look busy, so make busyness expensive to fake. Each identity keeps a signal log: every epoch it must finish one job for a stranger — a code review, a translation, a bug triage — and the client signs the result. The vine of signed jobs is the identity; cut off from real clients it withers, and records older than twelve epochs stop counting. A thousand fakes need a thousand finished jobs per epoch, about two thousand hours of real work, and any fake wandering between jobs without finishing one forfeits a 40 POA deposit.
